missing_external_entities.title: {count} required entities are missing
missing_external_entities.description:
The area_lighting integration expects the following entities to exist in Home Assistant, but they are missing:

{missing_list}

Without these, features depending on them are disabled or degraded (holiday detection, ambient zones, motion lighting).

### Copy-paste bootstrap

Add this to your `configuration.yaml` (or a package file) to create the missing helpers:

```yaml
{bootstrap_yaml}
```

After saving the file, reload the affected integrations or restart Home Assistant. See the component README for full setup details.

lutron_remotes_missing.title: {count} Lutron remotes have missing devices
lutron_remotes_missing.description:
The following Lutron remotes have device ids that no longer exist in Home Assistant. Their button presses are being ignored:

{remote_list}

A device id can change when a device is re-added or when Home Assistant 2026.8 split devices shared by multiple integrations.

Open Settings → Devices & services → Devices → the remote. The current device id is in the page URL. Update each remote's `id` under `lutron_remotes` in your configuration and restart Home Assistant.

scene_drift_unhealable.title: {area}: a light keeps drifting from its scene
scene_drift_unhealable.description: Home Assistant repeatedly tried to restore `{entity}` in {area} to its active scene, but it keeps changing back on its own. This usually means a Philips Hue power-on default, a Zigbee/RF dropout, or a Hue-app automation is driving the bulb independently of Home Assistant. Check the bulb's power-on behavior (set it to 'last state') and disable any competing Hue motion/automation for this room. The area has been left in `manual` until the next motion or remote event.

lighting_on.name: Turn on area lighting
lighting_on.description: Turns on lighting for an area, cycling through scenes intelligently based on the current state, holiday mode, night mode, and sun position.

lighting_off.name: Turn off area lighting
lighting_off.description: Turns off lighting for an area. Falls back to the ambient scene when ambience is enabled and the area isn't already in an ambience-owned state.

lighting_off_fade.name: Fade off area lighting
lighting_off_fade.description: Turns off lighting for an area with a fade transition. Used by motion/occupancy timer expiry.

lighting_favorite.name: Activate favorite scene
lighting_favorite.description: Activates the favorite scene for an area. Cycles between the active holiday scene (if any) and the night scene.

lighting_raise.name: Raise area brightness
lighting_raise.description: Raises the lights that are on in the area. The brightest moves up by the area's brightness step and the others keep their brightness relative to it. In a dark area, turns the remembered scene's lights on at the step level. Marks the area as dimmed without losing its scene identity.

lighting_lower.name: Lower area brightness
lighting_lower.description: Lowers the lights that are on in the area. The brightest moves down by the area's brightness step and the others keep their brightness relative to it, and once the brightest would reach zero they all turn off. In a dark area, turns the remembered scene's lights on at the step level, as raise does. Marks the area as dimmed without losing its scene identity.

lighting_circadian.name: Activate circadian lighting
lighting_circadian.description: Activates circadian lighting for an area. area_lighting sets each grouped light's brightness and color temperature from the sun and keeps them updated.

snapshot_scene.name: Snapshot area scene
snapshot_scene.description: Captures the current light states in an area and saves them as the definition for the named scene. Adjust lights to the desired levels before calling this.

scene.name: Scene slug
scene.description: The scene slug to overwrite (e.g., daylight, evening, night, ambient).

alert.name: Alert
alert.description: Flash lights in an area using a named alert pattern.

area_id.name: Area ID
area_id.description: The area ID, or "all" to alert every area.

pattern.name: Pattern
pattern.description: Name of the alert pattern defined in alert_patterns.

reload.name: Reload
reload.description: Re-reads the area_lighting YAML and applies it to running areas, adding and removing areas and scenes. Running areas keep their state and timers.
